newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania to meet IMF demands to revive economy.
newsitem.headline: Albania to meet IMF demands to revive economy.

text.p: Albania said on Tuesday that strict adherence to International Monetary Fund and World Bank programmes was the only hope for rebuilding its shattered economy after months of anarchy.

"We are determined to meet IMF demands, namely to restore order, boost the financial system and improve transparency regarding pyramid investment schemes," Finance Minister Arben Malaj told a news conference.

Malaj said the World Bank and other key donors had worked out an extensive programme which would help lift the country out of its deep economic crisis and open the way to large-scale investment from foreign institutions.

The international community, which helped Albania stage elections to end chaos after protests at collapsed pyramid schemes degenerated into violence, has pledged social, economic and military aid to Europe's poorest nation.
More than 1,500 people have been killed in the former communist country since unrest erupted in March.
The finance minister said the IMF had also elaborated a "programme of post-conflict reconstruction" aimed at creating conditions for massive economic and financial aid.
"After Bosnia and Georgia, we are the third country in the IMF history to benefit from such a programme and it is vital to convince foreign investors to invest in Albania," said Malaj.

The finance ministry's top priority will be to revive the financial system, taking control of customs duties and cutting public spending in order to narrow the budget deficit within six months to one year at the most.
Since February large swathes of the country have been out of government control, which has meant the authorities have been unable to collect many customs duties and taxes.

"We urge the parliament to approve draft laws on budget restrictions, fiscal elements and restoration of public order, so that we sign either a one-year standby agreement or a three-year accord with the IMF ," Malaj said.
Albania's parliament voted last month to audit the nation's surviving high-interest investment schemes and examine defunct pyramid schemes in a bid to return some of the population's lost savings.
The law stipulates that the administrators will have full jurisdiction over the activities and assets of firms offering high returns to depositors but it excludes already collapsed pyramid schemes.

"All we want is to persuade the conference of donors in Brussels, due in October that we are seriously working to rebuild our country and that we have not turned a blind eye on their proposals," Malaj said.
